requested_outcome: Make long Biz report pulls materially faster, visibly understandable, and durably attributable to the admin who started them.
natural_destination: The authenticated VII business-performance administration report.
authorization_boundary: Implement and verify in the current candidate. Production publication still requires an explicit deploy instruction and verified production route.

lesson_bundle.reason: The admin must behave as an operational product with durable history.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require actor, range, status, progress, reload and permission evidence.

lesson_bundle.reason: A faster loop must also prove failure and interruption behavior.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Test completion, stop, reload, failure counts and the affected report family.

lesson_bundle.reason: The operator needs one current progress view and one next action.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Show a clear percentage, counts and a compact history instead of raw background requests.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The month pull is still serial enough to take around twenty minutes.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Increase bounded supplier fan-out from four to twelve targets per wave while keeping wave boundaries.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Source and tests prove twelve-target waves and a twelve-target server cap.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The operator sees only a spinner and cannot tell if work is moving.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Render completed count, total and percentage as the batch advances.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The report contains a semantic progress visualization tied to live batch state.

predicted_rejections.rejection: A reload loses who ran the report and what happened.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Persist every run with actor, date range, scope, force flag, progress, result counts and timestamps.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: A new report request returns the stored history for all authorized admins.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Stopping one admin's job can stop another admin's run.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Bind stop and progress writes to both job ID and normalized actor email.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: A different actor cannot stop the stored run in the ownership test.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The system claims it can reconstruct the already-finished legacy action.
predicted_rejections.prevention: State that history starts when the durable audit version is deployed and never fabricate prior events.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: No synthetic historic run is inserted or displayed.

affected_family: Biz summary pulls for vacations, events and hourly rooms.
Business-performance batch progress, stop and reload states.
Authorized administration users and shared run history.

sources.label: VII platform operations and audit rules

midpoint_gate.trigger: The first persisted report run can be read after a new request.
checks: Verify actor, range, scope, status and result counts survive reload.
Verify the same UI presents bounded progress rather than an indefinite spinner.

attack_questions: Can a different admin stop the run?
Can a repeated chunk reduce or double-count progress?
Does an interrupted run falsely appear completed?
Did higher concurrency remove the server-side cap?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Open the authenticated business-performance report and inspect progress and history after starting, stopping and reloading a run.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Run report history, conversion cache, admin permission, full regression and production build checks.

effectiveness.baseline: Four businesses per sequential wave and no durable run history or progress visualization.
effectiveness.target: Three times the bounded parallelism, durable per-user run history and a truthful progress view without supplier overload or permission regression.
